memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are completed, for your ordination will last seven days. What has been done today was commanded by the LORD to make atonement for you.'" - Lev 8:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seven days. A full week of staying put at the entrance of the tent, before any ministry begins.

They had been washed, robed, anointed, and marked with blood. Everything was technically complete. And God said: wait.

This is a pattern He uses often. Moses spent forty years in the desert before Sinai. David was anointed king and then spent years running from Saul. Paul was converted and then went to Arabia. Jesus told His disciples to stay in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high (Lk 24:49) — after three years of training and a resurrection, they still had to wait.

Waiting is not wasted. It is where calling becomes character.

There is a particular danger in being newly equipped. A person who has just been gifted, appointed, or entrusted with something is often at their most eager and their least ready. The seven days protected Aaron from himself.

If God has shown you something He intends to do with your life and nothing seems to be happening yet, you may not be delayed. You may be at the entrance to the tent, exactly where He has told you to stay.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I in a season of waiting, and how am I handling it?
2. What might God be forming in me that could only be formed by waiting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to wait well. If You have told me to stay at the entrance, give me patience to remain there until You send me out. Amen.
